issues.legal_issue: A negotiated settlement of property disputes is not a decision by a nominated adjudicator merely because it is labelled a decision.
material_facts: The governing covenants provided for property disputes to be referred to a person nominated by the Government of India, whose decision would be final and binding.
No person was nominated to decide the dispute, and no such person issued a decision.
The ruler and the Ministry of States discussed the inventory, and the communication forwarding it described its settlement as part of an overall agreement concerning outstanding disputes.
issues.conclusion: The inventory recorded a mutual agreement between the ruler and the Government of India, not a decision by a person nominated under the covenants.
issues.legal_principle: The covenants required referral to a person nominated by the Government of India for a binding adjudication. Because no such person was nominated, and the communication described a negotiated settlement forming part of an overall agreement, the inventory was an agreement simpliciter despite being labelled a decision. The Court relied on Article XI(3) of the Matsya Covenant and Article XII(2) of the Rajasthan Covenant; it cited no earlier cases on this issue.

rule.if: property_status_dispute and inventory_discussed_in_negotiations and no_government_nominee and letter_describes_overall_settlement

predicates.property_status_dispute: The parties disputed whether items of property belonged privately to a ruler or to the state.
predicates.inventory_discussed_in_negotiations: The ruler and government representatives discussed an inventory of property claimed as private property.
predicates.no_government_nominee: The government did not nominate a person to adjudicate the property dispute.
predicates.letter_describes_overall_settlement: The communication forwarding the inventory described its settlement as part of an overall agreement on outstanding disputes.

issues.definition: When a property-status dispute is negotiated without a government-nominated adjudicator and the inventory is described as part of an overall settlement, the inventory records a mutual agreement.

issues.legal_issue: The constitutional bar on court jurisdiction applies to disputes arising from a pre-constitutional agreement between a ruler and the Government of India, including an agreement made pursuant to an earlier covenant.
material_facts: A ruler and the Government of India reached a property settlement before the Constitution commenced.
The settlement followed earlier covenants concerning the merger of states and the resolution of property disputes.
The ruler brought civil suits seeking recognition of property rights and rent or related relief based on the settlement.
issues.conclusion: The dispute arose from an agreement covered by Article 363, so the courts had no jurisdiction to entertain the claim.
issues.legal_principle: Article 363 bars court jurisdiction over disputes arising from a pre-constitutional treaty, agreement, covenant, or similar instrument made by a ruler of an Indian State to which the Government of India or a predecessor government was a party and which continued in operation after the Constitution commenced. The bar is not limited to a parent covenant; it also covers a later agreement made pursuant to an earlier agreement. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

rule.if: civil_property_claim_from_ruler_agreement and agreement_precedes_constitution and government_was_party and agreement_continued_after_constitution and agreement_followed_prior_covenant and claim_arises_from_agreement

predicates.civil_property_claim_from_ruler_agreemen: A ruler or a person claiming through a ruler brings a civil claim concerning property rights under an agreement.
predicates.agreement_precedes_constitution: The agreement was made before the Constitution commenced.
predicates.government_was_party: The Government of India or a predecessor government was a party to the agreement.
predicates.agreement_continued_after_constitution: The agreement continued in operation after the Constitution commenced.
predicates.agreement_followed_prior_covenant: The agreement was made pursuant to an earlier covenant or agreement.
predicates.claim_arises_from_agreement: The civil claim depends on rights or obligations said to arise from the agreement.

issues.definition: If a civil property claim depends on a pre-constitutional agreement made with the government, continued after the Constitution commenced, and made pursuant to an earlier covenant, courts lack jurisdiction over the claim.

issues.legal_issue: An inventory expressly made part of an overall settlement of outstanding disputes is not a final settlement standing by itself before the overall agreement is reached.
material_facts: The communication forwarding the inventory stated that settling it was an integral part of an overall agreement on outstanding disputes and that it did not stand by itself.
Outstanding property claims remained under consideration after the inventory was sent.
The parties later discussed the outstanding questions and reached a further settlement.
issues.conclusion: The inventory's terms were tentative and did not become final until the disputes were resolved as part of an overall agreed settlement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the communication as making the inventory settlement part of an overall agreement rather than a standalone final settlement. Accordingly, its terms could change while the settlement process continued, and finality attached only when all outstanding disputes were resolved by agreement. No earlier cases were relied on for this holding.

predicates.inventory_described_as_part_of_overall_s: The communication forwarding an inventory stated that its settlement was part of an overall agreement and did not stand alone.
predicates.outstanding_disputes_remained: Some disputes between the parties remained unresolved when the inventory was forwarded.
predicates.parties_later_reached_overall_settlement: The parties later discussed outstanding matters and reached a further settlement.

issues.definition: When an inventory is described as part of an overall settlement, disputes remain outstanding, and the parties later settle those matters together, the inventory's terms are tentative until that overall settlement.
